claim.text: Wikipedia permits editing anonymously without asking for identification or email. A study attributed to Dartmouth College in 2009 reportedly found, unexpectedly, that anonymous editors ranked among the leading producers of valid material on English Wikipedia.
claim.text_note: Public paraphrase. The original Wikipedia revision remains unrecorded.

sub_claims.note: Anonymous Editing. Later evidence review, with no subclaim verdict assigned: the study describes anonymous participation in its sample, which provides context but does not establish Wikipedia's editing policy.

sub_claims.text: Wikipedia editors do not have to provide identification or an email address.
sub_claims.note: Identification Requirements. Later evidence review, with no subclaim verdict assigned: the cited study does not establish either the identification or email requirement.

sub_claims.text: A study attributed to Dartmouth College in 2009 reportedly found, unexpectedly, that anonymous editors ranked among the leading producers of valid material on English Wikipedia.
sub_claims.note: Research Findings on Anonymous Contributions. Later evidence review, with no subclaim verdict assigned: the citation establishes the publication year. The recorded abstract passages do not establish Dartmouth College attribution or an English Wikipedia sample. They discuss the reliability of one-time anonymous contributions and do not establish relative contribution volume.
